key_insight: Explicitly enforcing person–garment correspondence within Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architectures enables much better preservation of fine garment details in virtual try-on, and CORAL shows how to induce and align these correspondences rather than leaving them to emerge implicitly.
problem_solved: Existing virtual try-on models—especially in unpaired settings—fail to preserve fine-grained garment details because they do not explicitly enforce or explain person↔garment correspondence inside DiT-based generators.
method: Analyze full 3D attention in Diffusion Transformers to reveal how and when person–garment correspondence emerges (diagnostic study of attention patterns).
Introduce CORAL, an alignment mechanism that supervises and guides DiT attention toward explicit person–garment correspondence (attention guidance + alignment loss / correspondence maps).
Integrate CORAL into a DiT-based VTON pipeline to produce higher-fidelity try-on results that retain texture, seams, and fine shape details in unpaired scenarios.
impact: CORAL improves realism and controllability of virtual try-on systems and offers a practical recipe for practitioners to enforce and interpret correspondence in attention-based generative models, making DiT-based synthesis more reliable for garment-aware applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side before/after try-on images highlighting preserved textures and seams (baseline vs CORAL).
Attention-map overlays showing emergent vs. CORAL-aligned person→garment correspondences.
Block diagram of the DiT-based VTON pipeline with the CORAL module and alignment loss annotated.
Bar chart or table summarizing improvements on key fidelity/compatibility metrics (e.g., texture, shape, user preference).
paper_title: CORAL: Correspondence Alignment for Improved Virtual Try-On
paper_authors: Jiyoung Kim, Youngjin Shin, Siyoon Jin, Dahyun Chung, Jisu Nam
